ALL.name: The Allstate Corporation
ALL.business: US personal property & casualty insurer (auto, homeowners) plus protection products.

news.title: Q2 adj. net income $8.99/share (+46%); $1.0B buyback in the quarter
August catastrophe losses $748M pre-tax; Jul+Aug $1.43B

pros: Cheap: forward P/E 8.3 (Yahoo)
Auto profitability restored; ROE 46.1%
Large buybacks ($2.6B left on the $4B authorization)
cons: Volatile catastrophe losses: Jul+Aug already $1.43B pre-tax
Auto-insurance pricing tailwind may fade as margins normalize
ALL.take: Cheap, cash-returning insurer at peak profitability; cats and a softening pricing cycle are the risks.

AMGN.name: Amgen Inc.
AMGN.business: Large-cap biopharma: Repatha, Prolia/Xgeva, Evenity, Tezspire, oncology and biosimilars; MariTide obesity drug in Phase 3.

news.title: Q2 revenue $10.1B (+10%), non-GAAP EPS $6.29; FY26 guide $38.2–39.4B revenue
Pipeline update: MariTide Phase 3 (MARITIME) enrolling strongly; key obesity readouts ~2027

pros: Steady growth (+10%) with operating margin 35.5% (Yahoo)
Huge free cash flow ($8.65B); dividend yield 2.5%
Obesity optionality (MariTide) plus Imdelltra/Tezspire growth
cons: Price already above the analyst mean target $391; consensus 'hold'
Biosimilar erosion (Prolia/Xgeva) and drug-pricing policy risk
AMGN.take: Defensive cash machine with an obesity call option; fair value, not a bargain — fine as a pullback trade, weak as a fundamental upside case.

ARMK.name: Aramark
ARMK.business: Food and facilities services for education, healthcare, business, sports & entertainment and corrections clients.

news.title: Fiscal Q3 revenue $5.1B (+9% organic); FY26 organic growth guide raised to 9–10%; record client wins
S&P upgrades credit ratings; Moody's outlook to positive

pros: Organic growth 9–10% with ~98% retention
EPS growth guide +20–25%; credit upgrades
Analyst consensus 'strong buy', mean target $68 (Yahoo)
cons: Forward P/E 19.7 for a low-margin services business
ARMK.take: Steady contract-services grower deleveraging toward upgrades; fundamentals supportive, low margins cap the upside.

ATI.name: ATI Inc.
ATI.business: Specialty materials: titanium, nickel-based alloys and forgings, mainly for jet engines, airframes and defense.

news.title: Q2: FY26 guide raised (adj. EBITDA $1.135–1.185B, EPS $4.90–5.18, FCF $550–600M); record $4.4B backlog
Morgan Stanley Laguna conference: targets ~$1.35B EBITDA run-rate entering 2027

pros: Aerospace & defense ~70% of revenue; defense sales +90% y/y
Margin expansion (adj. EBITDA margin 22.6%) and pricing resets
Analyst consensus 'strong buy', mean target $256 (Yahoo)
ATI.take: Strong aerospace up-cycle story with rising margins; fundamentals back the trend, valuation leaves little room for a miss.

BWA.name: BorgWarner Inc.
BWA.business: Turbochargers, drivetrain/Morse chains, eMotors, inverters and battery systems for combustion, hybrid and EV makers; developing TurboCell turbine generators for data-center power.

news.title: Morgan Stanley upgrades to Overweight, target $71→$95 on TurboCell AI-power opportunity; shares +~5%
J.P. Morgan sets $85 target, Buy
Q2: adj. EPS $1.42 (+17%), FY26 adj. EPS guide raised to $5.05–5.30, buyback +$1B

pros: Cheap: forward P/E 10.4, P/S 0.9 (Yahoo)
Margin expansion despite flat sales: Q2 adj. operating margin 11.3% (+100 bp)
Shareholder returns: ~$1.35B buyback authorization through 2029
Optional upside from data-center power (TurboCell deliveries expected 2027)
cons: No top-line growth: FY26 organic sales guided −1.5% to −3.5% (battery business shrinking)
Cyclical auto-production exposure; estimates were trending down after Q2 (Zacks)
TurboCell is pre-revenue; the AI-power story could fade
BWA.take: Value auto supplier with improving margins and a buyback, plus an AI-power call option — fundamentals support a pullback buy, but growth is not the story.

FTI.name: TechnipFMC plc
FTI.business: Subsea oil & gas systems (integrated iEPCI projects, Subsea 2.0 equipment, flexible pipe) and Surface Technologies.

news.title: Q2: inbound orders $2.73B, backlog $16.44B; 2026 subsea guide reaffirmed, ~$10B subsea orders targeted
iEPCI award for PETRONAS Limbayong deepwater project ($75–250M)
Petrobras flexible-flowline contract ($75–250M)

pros: Huge visibility: $16.4B backlog, steady subsea awards
Strong cash generation: free cash flow $1.46B, ROE 35.8% (Yahoo)
Subsea margin guide 21–22% adj. EBITDA
cons: Forward P/E 19.3 is not cheap for an oilfield name (Yahoo)
FTI.take: Best-in-class subsea franchise with locked-in backlog; buy-the-dip case is solid as long as offshore spending holds.

GL.name: Globe Life Inc.
GL.business: Life and supplemental health insurance sold to middle-income US households (American Income Life, Family Heritage, direct-to-consumer).

news.title: Q2 net operating EPS $3.61 (+10%); FY26 operating EPS guide raised to $15.55–15.95; $175M buyback
Q2 recap: stock fell ~7% after the release despite the beat

pros: Cheap: forward P/E 10.0 (Yahoo)
Steady growth: premiums +7%, health premium +16%
Consistent buybacks; ROE 20.9%; SEC/DOJ probes into AIL sales practices closed without enforcement action
cons: Remaining civil/derivative litigation and agent-practice headline risk
Life premium growth only +3%; agent recruiting is the key swing factor
GL.take: Fundamentally cheap, steady compounder; the discount reflects lingering reputation/legal risk rather than weak numbers.

IESC.name: IES Holdings, Inc.
IESC.business: Electrical and technology infrastructure contractor: Communications, Infrastructure Solutions, Commercial & Industrial and Residential segments; data centers are the main driver.

news.title: Fiscal Q3: revenue $1.243B (+40%), operating income +60%; backlog $4.5B (+91% since FY25 end)
2-for-1 stock split goes ex-date (announced Jul 31)

pros: Hyper-growth: revenue +40%, C&I segment +109% on data centers
Record $4.5B backlog gives visibility into FY27
Net cash: $388M cash vs $77M debt; ROE 44.5% (Yahoo)
cons: Heavy dependence on data-center capex — any slowdown hits 3 of 4 segments
Residential segment weak (housing starts, margin pressure)
Q3 helped by quick-turn jobs and a $26M securities gain; labor availability is a constraint
P/S 3.2 after a big run (52w range 170.06–408.25) (Yahoo)
IESC.take: Best growth profile in the group with a net-cash balance sheet; the risk is data-center cycle sentiment, not fundamentals.

INCY.name: Incyte Corporation
INCY.business: Biopharma: Jakafi (myelofibrosis/PV), Opzelura cream (vitiligo, eczema), plus an oncology/dermatology pipeline (povorcitinib).

news.title: Q2 revenue $1.674B (+38%); FY26 net sales guide $5.13–5.26B, Opzelura raised to $1.05–1.10B
Conference: Jakafi XR expected to retain ~$750M through the Jakafi patent transition

pros: Low valuation: forward P/E 12.9 (Yahoo)
Fortress balance sheet: $4.54B cash, almost no debt
Growth +38% with operating margin 41.9%; povorcitinib US launch expected Q1 2027
cons: Jakafi patent cliff — the core franchise faces generics
Part of 2026 Opzelura sales from a one-off CMS settlement ($300–310M)
Binary pipeline readouts (HS / prurigo nodularis Phase 3 in Q4)
INCY.take: Cheap, cash-rich biotech growing fast now, but the stock is a bet that the pipeline outruns the Jakafi cliff.

IRM.name: Iron Mountain Inc.
IRM.business: Specialty REIT: records/information storage plus fast-growing data centers, asset lifecycle management (ALM) and digital solutions.

news.title: Q2 revenue $2.03B (+18.5%), AFFO/share $1.44 (+16%); FY26 guidance raised
CFO at Goldman conference: growth portfolio to expand >20%; ~$1B data-center revenue this year
Upgraded to Strong-Buy at Rothschild & Co Redburn

pros: Growth businesses (data centers, ALM, digital) up >50% y/y; 110 MW leased YTD
Guidance raised across revenue, EBITDA and AFFO
Dividend yield 3.1%; analyst mean target $145 (Yahoo)
cons: Heavy leverage: ~$19.95B debt vs $205M cash; negative free cash flow from the build-out (Yahoo)
Expensive on earnings: forward P/E 41.6 (REIT — AFFO is the better yardstick)
Rate-sensitive; leasable data-center land bank shrinking (325 MW)
IRM.take: A legacy storage cash cow funding a data-center growth engine — strong momentum, but leverage and rates are the swing factors.

LAMR.name: Lamar Advertising Company
LAMR.business: Outdoor-advertising REIT: billboards (incl. digital), transit and logo signs across the US and Canada.

news.title: Q2 AFFO/share $2.40 (+8.1%); FY26 AFFO/share guide raised to $8.75–8.90
Declares $1.65/share quarterly dividend
Shares slide with REITs as Treasury yields rise

pros: Raised AFFO guidance; dividend yield 4.6% (Yahoo)
High margins: operating margin 33.3%
Digital billboard conversion supports pricing
cons: Ad spending is cyclical; growth only mid-single-digit (rev +6.5%)
LAMR.take: Stable income REIT with raised guidance; upside depends mostly on rates, so fundamentals are a mild plus, not a driver.

LFUS.name: Littelfuse, Inc.
LFUS.business: Circuit protection (fuses, TVS), power semiconductors and sensors for industrial, data-center, automotive and electronics markets.

news.title: Q2 sales $739M (+20%, +14% organic), adj. EPS $4.19; industrial +52% on data centers
Senior leadership transition: Electronics + Semiconductor businesses combined under one leader from Jan 2027

pros: Growth re-accelerating (+20% sales) with data-center tailwind
High-voltage data-center design wins scaling from 2027
Modest leverage (debt $709M vs cash $631M) (Yahoo)
cons: Trailing GAAP net margin slightly negative (-0.3%) (Yahoo)
LFUS.take: Cyclical recovery plus a data-center story; fundamentals improving, valuation fair — a reasonable pullback buy.

MOG-A.name: Moog Inc. (Class A)
MOG-A.business: Precision motion and fluid controls for military/commercial aircraft, space & defense and industrial markets (incl. data-center cooling).

news.title: Record fiscal Q3: sales $1.117B (+15%), adj. EPS $3.72; FY26 guide raised to $4.4B sales / $11.65 adj. EPS
12-month backlog $3.3B, up 23%
$16.5M Navy V-22 swashplate actuator overhaul award

pros: Double-digit growth: Q3 sales +15%, backlog +23%
FY26 guidance raised on every metric (adj. op. margin 14.1% vs 13.4%)
Defense + commercial aero up-cycle; ROE 18.1% (Yahoo)
cons: FY26 EPS raise partly one-offs (IEEPA tariff refund $30M, R&D tax credits)
MOG-A.take: Quality aerospace/defense compounder with real momentum; valuation and one-off-boosted EPS argue for buying only near support.

PH.name: Parker-Hannifin Corporation
PH.business: Motion and control technologies: aerospace systems, hydraulics, filtration, fluid connectors.

news.title: Record fiscal Q4: sales $5.8B (+9.8%), adj. EPS $9.27; orders +19%; FY27 adj. EPS guide $34.25–35.25
Completes $9.25B Filtration Group acquisition (~$1.8B FY27 sales, EPS accretive)

pros: Record backlog $12.8B; orders accelerating
Margin leader: operating margin 23.5% (Yahoo)
Aerospace + filtration mix shift supports multiple
cons: Debt $8.73B rises with the Filtration Group deal
PH.take: Top-tier industrial compounder; strong fundamentals, premium price. (Only graded with a larger account — 1 share > position cap.)

RHP.name: Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc.
RHP.business: Lodging REIT owning large group-meeting resorts (Gaylord Hotels, JW Marriott/Ritz-Carlton) plus Opry Entertainment.

news.title: Q2 beat; FY26 same-store RevPAR growth guide raised to 3.5–4.5%
Closes $1.38B Grande Lakes Orlando acquisition; updates 2026 outlook
Declares $1.20 Q3 dividend

pros: Group-meeting demand strong; guidance raised
Acquisitive growth (Grande Lakes)
Dividend yield 4.0%; consensus 'strong buy', mean target $140 (Yahoo)
cons: Leverage: debt $4.13B (Yahoo), more after the acquisition
Possible sale of the Entertainment segment adds uncertainty
RHP.take: Well-run group-hotel REIT with raised guidance and analyst support; leverage and the travel cycle are the main risks.

ROK.name: Rockwell Automation, Inc.
ROK.business: Industrial automation: PLCs/controllers, drives, motion, software and lifecycle services.

news.title: Fiscal Q3: FY26 guide raised — sales +7.5–9.5%, adj. EPS $13.00–13.30
Goldman cuts target to $485; Deutsche Bank raises to $500

pros: Recovery in industrial automation; guidance raised
Strong FCF ($1.30B, ~100% conversion target)
Operating margin 21.0%; ROE 30.6% (Yahoo)
cons: Mixed analyst views (consensus near hold, Wells Fargo Equal Weight)
ROK.take: High-quality cyclical in recovery mode; the fundamentals are fine but already priced — rely on the chart setup.

ROST.name: Ross Stores, Inc.
ROST.business: Off-price apparel and home retailer (Ross Dress for Less, dd's DISCOUNTS).

news.title: Q2 sales $6.27B (+13%), comps +10%; FY EPS guide raised to $8.61–8.77; 115 new stores planned
Consensus 'Moderate Buy'; several targets raised (e.g. Truist $310)

pros: Strong comps (+10%) and store growth
Large cash pile: $4.29B cash vs $4.74B total debt (Yahoo)
ROE 42.6%; off-price wins in a cautious consumer environment
cons: Q2 EPS included ~$0.60 tariff refunds — not recurring
H2 comps guided lower (6–7% Q3, 4–5% Q4)
ROST.take: Fundamentally strong retailer with momentum; the one-off tariff boost and a full multiple are the caveats.

ST.name: Sensata Technologies Holding plc
ST.business: Sensors, electrical protection and power-distribution components for automotive, heavy-vehicle, industrial and aerospace markets.

news.title: Launches OmniNode high-voltage power-distribution platform for commercial EVs
Barclays upgrades to Overweight, $55 target

pros: Cheap on forward earnings: forward P/E 10.3, P/S 1.6 (Yahoo)
Earnings growing faster than sales (adj. EPS +12.6%)
Solid free cash flow ($504M) supports deleveraging/buybacks
cons: GAAP margin thin (net margin 2.4%); trailing P/E 70.2
ST.take: Value/self-help story with an analyst upgrade tailwind; fundamentals are adequate but not a growth reason to own it.

SWK.name: Stanley Black & Decker, Inc.
SWK.business: Power tools and hand tools (DEWALT, STANLEY, CRAFTSMAN) and engineered fastening.

news.title: Q2 sales $4.0B (flat, +3% organic), adj. EPS $1.57; FY26 adj. EPS guide raised to $5.20–5.80
Agrees to sell Excel Industries (Hustler mowers, ~$300M revenue) to Bad Boy Mowers

pros: Turnaround: guidance raised, portfolio pruning continues
Valuation: forward P/E 13.8, P/S 0.9; dividend yield 3.8% (Yahoo)
Free cash flow guide raised to $600–800M
cons: No growth: sales flat y/y (+3% organic)
Tariff exposure; Q2 EPS included a $0.17 tariff-refund benefit
SWK.take: Cheap turnaround with a high yield, but sales are not growing — a fundamentals-neutral name; trade it on the chart.

URI.name: United Rentals, Inc.
URI.business: Largest US equipment-rental company (general and specialty rentals).

news.title: Record Q2: revenue $4.4B, adj. EPS $12.76; FY26 revenue guide raised to $17.5–17.8B
Management: large-project pipeline accelerating, specialty demand strong

pros: Mega-project demand (data centers, manufacturing) driving raised guidance
Strong FCF ($1.71B) funds buybacks/M&A (Yahoo)
Forward P/E 18.3
cons: Diesel cost $5.34/gal YTD vs $3.66 a year earlier
URI.take: Cycle leader with raised guidance and a long project pipeline; fundamentals supportive. (Only graded with a larger account — 1 share > position cap.)

WELL.name: Welltower Inc.
WELL.business: Healthcare REIT focused on senior housing (operating portfolio), plus outpatient medical properties in the US, Canada and UK.

news.title: Q2: FY26 normalized FFO guide raised to $6.36–6.44/share
Jefferies starts at Strong-Buy; JPMorgan upgrade to Overweight ($260)

pros: Senior-housing demographic tailwind; revenue +39.1% y/y (Yahoo)
FFO guidance raised; active acquirer (Amica portfolio)
Moderate leverage: debt/equity 41% (Yahoo)
cons: Very expensive: forward P/E 70.7, P/S 12.7 (Yahoo) — premium REIT multiple
Rate-sensitive; acquisition-driven growth carries execution risk
WELL.take: Best-in-class senior-housing growth REIT with analyst momentum; fundamentals strong but the premium multiple limits margin of safety.

WTS.name: Watts Water Technologies, Inc.
WTS.business: Plumbing, heating, water-quality and flow-control products (valves, boilers, thermal storage) for commercial and residential buildings.

news.title: Record Q2: sales $763M (+19%, +12% organic), adj. EPS $3.66; FY26 sales outlook raised (8–11% organic)
Data-center sales more than tripled y/y; data-center TAM estimate roughly doubled to ~$2B

pros: Double-digit organic growth with pricing power (~6% price)
New data-center leg (CoolVault thermal storage) adds a secular driver
Net cash ($348M cash vs $212M debt); operating margin 20.9% (Yahoo)
cons: Adj. operating margin −60 bp (acquisition dilution, tariffs/inflation)
Part of Q2 demand was pull-forward; Middle East softness
WTS.take: High-quality industrial with a balance-sheet cushion and a data-center kicker; fundamentals fine, valuation already prices quality.
